title: Finite-type domains for an open restriction of the fixed square
statement: Let $k$ be the algebraically closed field of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $X,C$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $c:C\to Z=X\times_sX$ be a $k$-morphism, $\Delta:X\to Z$ its diagonal, and $F=C\times_{Z,c,\Delta}X$ with projections $i:F\to C$, $d:F\to X$ [def-trf-fixed-scheme]. For an open immersion $j:W\hookrightarrow C$ [def-weil-open-immersion], form $F_W=W\times_C F$ with projections $i_W:F_W\to W$ and $j':F_W\to F$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $Z,W,F,F_W$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes; $i,i_W$ are closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $j'$ is an open immersion. The maps $c,cj,\Delta,i,d,i_W,j,j',dj'$, the two projections $Z\to X$, and all structure maps to $s$ are separated and of finite type. No reducedness or properness of $C,W,F,F_W$ is assumed.

source.place: §0.2 and §1.2.1: geometric domains of the two pasted fixed squares (auxiliary scheme lemma).

proof.text: Write $a_X:X\to s$ and $a_C:C\to s$ for the structure maps. The spectrum of the field $k$ is Noetherian: its one-point space is quasi-compact and its local ring is a field, whose only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$. Thus $s$ is Noetherian; the finite-type maps $a_X,a_C$ therefore make $X$ and $C$ Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The product $Z=X\times_sX$ has projections $p_1,p_2$. Each projection is the base change of the separated finite-type structure map $a_X$, so it is separated and of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Composing $p_1$ with $a_X$ gives the structure map of $Z$, which is separated and finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] and clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Thus $Z$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, and both projections have the asserted properties.

Factor $c$ as $C\xrightarrow{\gamma=(1,c)}C\times_s Z\xrightarrow{p_Z}Z$. The graph square with bottom map $\Delta_Z:Z\to Z\times_sZ$ and right map $(c\,p_C,p_Z):C\times_s Z\to Z\times_sZ$ is Cartesian: on maps from any scheme $T$, its equation says precisely that the second coordinate is $c$ of the first; the inverse to the resulting identification with $C$ is $p_C$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Since $Z$ is separated, $\Delta_Z$ is closed [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $\gamma$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] and hence separated and finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. The projection $p_Z$ is the base change of $a_C$ and is separated finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Their composite $c$ is separated finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e) and [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. This is the elementary pullback proof of the graph assertion of Stacks Tag 01KS (lemma-semi-diagonal).

source.place: Tag 01KS, lemma-semi-diagonal, with its fibre-product proof written out; separated finite-type permanence as cited

proof.text: The diagonal $\Delta:X\to Z$ is a closed immersion because $X\to s$ is separated, by the definition in [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Hence $\Delta$ is proper, in particular separated and of finite type, by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. The fixed square in [def-trf-fixed-scheme] is the pullback of $\Delta$ along $c$: therefore $i:F\to C$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The same closed-immersion-proper node makes $i$ separated and of finite type. The other projection $d:F\to X$ is the base change of $c$, so it is separated and of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Composing either projection with the relevant finite-type structure map shows that $F$ is separated and finite type over $s$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e).

Because $C$ is Noetherian, its open subscheme $W$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. More precisely, for every affine open $V\subset C$, $j^{-1}(V)$ is an open subscheme of $C$ and the same node makes it quasi-compact. Hence $j$ is a quasi-compact morphism, so [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] makes it finite type. An open immersion is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation](a). Composing $j$ with $a_C$ and with $c$ now shows that $W\to s$ and $cj:W\to Z$ are separated finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e) and [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change].

proof.text: The defining square $F_W=W\times_C F$ is the pullback of $i$ along $j$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus $i_W:F_W\to W$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], hence separated and finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Composition with $W\to s$ shows that $F_W$ is separated finite type over $s$, using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e) and [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The projection $j':F_W\to F$ is the base change of $j$, hence an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and separated finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], since Step 4 proved these properties for $j$.

source.place: Tag 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion); morphisms.tex, Tags 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion), 01W5 (lemma-closed-immersion-proper), 01T3 and 01T4; schemes.tex, Tag 01KU.

proof.text: Finally $dj'$ is a composite of separated finite-type maps, so it is separated and of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e) and [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The maps $i,i_W,j,j',d,dj',c,cj,\Delta$ and the two product projections have now all been checked, and their composites with the structure maps are the stated structure maps to $s$. Every argument used only finite-type, separated, open, closed, and pullback permanence; no reducedness or properness of $C,W,F,F_W$ was introduced.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q14-66ab20ef3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery in full. It has no new nodes, and the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged (compared field by field with the side DAG). The six steps are correct against the cited statements. Step 1: Spec k is Noetherian, so X and C are Noetherian; the projections of Z are base changes of a_X. Step 2: I checked the Cartesian graph square by test points (b=z=c a), so (1,c) is the base change of the closed Delta_Z and c = p_Z(1,c); Stacks 01KS = lemma-semi-diagonal, which I read. Step 3: i is the base change of the closed Delta_X along c, as in def-trf-fixed-scheme and Varshavsky 1.2.1; d is the base change of c. Step 4: j is quasi-compact on every affine V because j^{-1}(V) is an open of the Noetherian C; it is then of finite type by the qc-open-immersion node and separated by cancellation (a). Step 5: i_W and j' are base changes of i and j, and the orientations match the nodes. Step 6: dj' is a composite. Every cited lemma is a Mathlib leaf or a definition, so the route is respected and no tool_uses are accepted. I checked the edge cases W empty, W=C, C empty, nonreduced C, non-proper C, and c with F=C. The duplicate search (fixed-square nodes, graph and closed-immersion nodes, 01KS) found no node with this content. The item states a geometric lemma the parent's step 2 needs, not a restated clause of the parent. No SGA source is used. Varshavsky 0.2, 1.1.9 and 1.2.1 were read.
